Before it became what we know as Pilates today, it was called “Contrology” a method created by Joseph Pilates.

His journey shaped the method.
As a child, he struggled with multiple health issues, which led him to deeply study the body, movement, and strength. During World War I, he worked with injured soldiers, using spring-based resistance to help them recover.. laying the foundation for what we now know as Pilates equipment.

When he later opened his studio in New York, Contrology became a space for healing, strength, and movement, especially among dancers and performers.

Contrology wasn’t just exercise.
It was a system of movement built on:

• breath
• control
• precision
• flow
• centering (the powerhouse)
• alignment

Every movement had intention.
Every transition had purpose.

He believed:
“It is the mind itself which builds the body.”

Over the years, Pilates has evolved & that evolution is important too.

Today, we understand more about biomechanics, rehabilitation, pelvic health, and the nervous system. This allows us to adapt the method for modern bodies.. making it more accessible, therapeutic, and relevant.

We modify. We personalise. We meet the body where it is. But the essence remains.

At its core, Pilates still teaches you how to move.
How to find your neutral spine,
engage your deep core,
move with control over momentum,
and connect breath with movement.

And that’s why I LOVEEEEE Pilates 😍

Because it goes beyond a workout.
It builds awareness that stays with you.. in how you move, sit, stand & live.

Simple, but never easy. Subtle, but deeply powerful.

On World Pilates Day, this is just a reminder of where it all began & why it still matters 🤍

If you truly love Pilates, read

If you are pregnant and have ever thought..
“What if I can’t handle labor pain?
What if it gets too intense?
What if I panic in that moment?
How will I even know what to do?”

You’re not alone. Almost every mom has these thoughts at some point.

And honestly, that’s because no one really explains how to use information during labor.

This is exactly where a labor & delivery session helps:

🔸 You understand what labor actually feels like and how it progresses, so you’re not second guessing every pain
🔸 You learn when to go to the hospital, instead of going too early or rushing in panic
🔸 You’re taught how to breathe and move during contractions, not just theoretically
🔸 You practice positions that can actually make labor smoother and more comfortable
🔸 You understand how to push, and more importantly, how to relax your pelvic floor at the right time
🔸 Your partner also knows how to support you, instead of feeling lost

It doesn’t make labor “easy” 
but it makes you feel much more in control of what’s happening.

And that changes the whole experience.

Because when you understand your body and trust the process,
things feel less overwhelming… and a lot more manageable 🤍

🚨 Most moms realise this only after delivery, don’t be one of them!

This pregnancy habit is not just “good for you”… it’s building your baby’s brain 🧠👶🏻 

There’s a powerful protein your body produces called
Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor

And it plays a key role in brain development.

🧠 What does BDNF actually do?

BDNF helps:
• Brain cells grow (neurogenesis)
• Form stronger connections (synapses)
• Function efficiently

👉🏼 In simple terms: it supports how the brain is built and wired

🤰🏻 Why does this matter in pregnancy?

Your baby’s brain is developing rapidly in the womb.

Higher BDNF levels are associated with:
• Better neuronal growth
• Improved brain connectivity
• Stronger foundation for learning & memory

🚶🏻‍♀️Where does exercise come in?

Research shows that exercise increases BDNF levels

When you move:
• Blood flow to the brain improves
• Oxygen & nutrients increase
• Your body signals the brain to release more BDNF

👉🏼 Creating a more supportive environment for your baby’s brain development

💛 Benefits for both mom & baby

For baby 👶🏻 
• Supports brain development
• Enhances neural connections

For mom 🤰🏻 
• Improves mood
• Reduces stress & anxiety
• Supports mental well-being

Exercise in pregnancy is not just about weight or fitness.
It is a neuroprotective and neurodevelopmental tool benefiting both maternal and fetal brain health.

📚 References 

• Erickson KI et al. Exercise training increases size of hippocampus and improves memory (PNAS, 2011)
• ACOG Committee Opinion No. 804: Physical Activity and Exercise During Pregnancy and the Postpartum Period
• Huang T et al. The effects of exercise on BDNF levels in humans (Neuroscience & Biobehavioral Reviews, 2014)

If you’re pregnant, this is your sign to move 💛
& if you know someone who is… send this to them right now 👶🏻

• Back & pelvic pain
• Urine leaks
• Poor stamina during labour

🤰🏻Pregnancy needs more than just walking.

And the right exercises depend on:
• Your trimester
• Your body type
• Your pregnancy symptoms

🔬Fertility testing is essential for diagnosing and addressing potential issues in women trying to conceive. It involves a series of evaluations to assess hormonal balance, ovarian function, and reproductive anatomy, providing a comprehensive understanding of a woman’s fertility status.✨

📌 Ovulation Monitoring🗓️
- Essential for tracking the release of an egg, helping to time conception accurately.

📌 Blood Tests💉
- Follicle-Stimulating Hormone (FSH): Assesses ovarian reserve and function.
- Luteinizing Hormone (LH): Diagnoses ovulation issues.
- Anti-Müllerian Hormone (AMH): Evaluates ovarian reserve.
- Estradiol (E2): Measures ovarian follicle health and hormonal balance.
- Progesterone (P): Confirms ovulation and luteal phase health.
- Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone (TSH): Detects thyroid disorders affecting fertility.
- Prolactin (PRL): Identifies hyperprolactinemia that can disrupt ovulation.

📌 Transvaginal Ultrasound🩺
- Antral Follicle Count (AFC): Estimates the number of remaining eggs.
- Ovarian Reserve: Assesses the quantity and quality of eggs.

📌 Hysterosalpingography (HSG)🩻
- Evaluates fallopian tube patency and uterine cavity for abnormalities.

❗️These comprehensive fertility tests are crucial for diagnosing underlying issues, guiding personalized treatment plans, and optimizing the chances of conception.🩷

💭 “Just do Kegels every day.. it’ll make labor easier!”
Sound familiar? 🙋🏻‍♀️ You’re definitely not alone.

👀 But here’s what most people don’t explain:
Your pelvic floor isn’t just about squeezing stronger. It also needs to relax, lengthen, and let go during birth.

➡️ For some, pelvic floor strengthening is helpful - yes, Kegels can improve support and prevent leaks.
➡️ But many pregnant women have pelvic floors that are tight or overactive… and doing more Kegels can actually make relaxing harder when it matters most 😮‍💨

✨ What really prepares you for birth is pelvic floor awareness, knowing when to contract and when to fully release.
Because during delivery, strength alone won’t cut it. Being able to let go is just as important.

👩🏻‍⚕️ As a pelvic health physio, I assess your individual pelvic floor needs and guide you through exercises that help your body get ready for labor the right way.. no unnecessary squeezing or guessing.

Most pregnancy advice falls into two extremes ❌
Over-resting or random, unguided workouts!🙄

And that’s exactly where most moms get stuck 😅

During pregnancy, the biggest mistakes I see are -

• ignoring pain thinking “this is normal”
• doing absolutely nothing because “better safe than sorry”
• or following random workouts/advice without knowing if it’s right for your body

Here’s the truth 🤓

🔸 Every pregnancy is different
🔸 What’s safe for one mom may not be right for another
🔸 Pain is information, not something to “push through”
🔸 Movement is important.. but the right kind, at the right time

It’s not about doing everything.
It’s about doing what’s right for YOU ✨
